heatwave_events.name: Heatwaves per year
heatwave_events.definition: Number of heatwaves a year. A heatwave is 3 or more days in a row that are unusually hot for that place.

heatwave_days.name: Heatwave days per year
heatwave_days.definition: Number of days a year that fall inside a heatwave (3 or more unusually hot days in a row).

longest_heatwave.name: Longest heatwave
longest_heatwave.definition: Length of the longest heatwave of the year, in days. Zero means the year had no heatwave.

first_heatwave_doy.name: Date of first heatwave
first_heatwave_doy.definition: The day of the year the first heatwave starts. A smaller number means heatwaves arrive earlier.

hottest_day.name: Hottest day of the year
hottest_day.definition: The highest daytime temperature reached in the year.

warm_nights.name: Warm nights per year
warm_nights.definition: Number of nights a year that stay unusually warm for that place, the kind that make sleep difficult.

summer_length.name: Length of summer
summer_length.definition: Number of days a year with summer-like warmth: a 5-day average temperature of 15 °C or more.

autumn_onset_doy.name: Start of autumn
autumn_onset_doy.definition: The day of the year autumn chill arrives: the first time after 1 July the 5-day average drops below 10 °C.

first_frost_doy.name: First frost
first_frost_doy.definition: The day of the year of the first autumn frost: the first night after 1 August at 0 °C or below.

wettest_day.name: Wettest day of the year
wettest_day.definition: The most rain that fell in a single day in the year.

heavy_rain_days.name: Heavy rain days per year
heavy_rain_days.definition: Number of days a year with 10 mm of rain or more, a properly wet day.

summer_dry_spell.name: Longest summer dry spell
summer_dry_spell.definition: The longest run of days in a row with under 1 mm of rain, in June to August.

winter_rain.name: Winter rainfall
winter_rain.definition: Total rain from December to February. The winter is named after the year its January falls in.

summer_sunshine.name: Summer sunshine
summer_sunshine.definition: Average sunlight energy reaching the ground each day in June to August. A higher number means sunnier, less cloudy summers.

heating_need.name: Heating need
heating_need.definition: How much heating a home needs over the year: for each day colder than 18.3 °C, the number of degrees below it is added up. A smaller number means less heating.

heatwave_events.caveat: 'Unusually hot' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer days for that place, so the temperature bar differs between towns.

heatwave_days.caveat: 'Unusually hot' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer days for that place, so the temperature bar differs between towns.

longest_heatwave.caveat: One long hot spell can dominate a year, so single years jump around a lot.

first_heatwave_doy.caveat: Years with no heatwave have no date and are left out, so this trend uses fewer years.

hottest_day.caveat: NASA values are averages over a roughly 50 km square, so peaks read lower than a city weather station.

warm_nights.caveat: 'Unusually warm' means the top 10% of 1981-2010 summer nights for that place.

summer_length.caveat: 15 °C is a fixed bar, so colder northern towns have short 'summers' by this measure.

autumn_onset_doy.caveat: A single early cold snap can pull the date forward in any one year.

first_frost_doy.caveat: Mild years with no frost before 31 December have no date and are left out. Local frost hollows are missed by 50 km data.

wettest_day.caveat: NASA values are averages over a roughly 50 km square, so a local downpour reads lower than a rain gauge under it.

heavy_rain_days.caveat: Rain swings a lot from one year to the next, so a trend needs to be large before it can be told apart from chance.

summer_dry_spell.caveat: One long dry spell can dominate a year (56 days in London in 2018), so single years jump around a lot.

winter_rain.caveat: The first winter is 1981-82, so 1981 has no value. Rain swings a lot from one year to the next.

summer_sunshine.caveat: NASA's sunshine record starts in 1984, so this trend covers 1984 to 2025.

heating_need.caveat: This counts cold weather only. Real heating bills also depend on insulation, wind and prices.
